title: Small simplicial-presheaf presentations of combinatorial model categories
statement:
Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the simplicial-set convention of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A model category here is complete and cocomplete, with weak equivalences $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three and closure under retracts, and classes $C,F$ such that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and a factorization of every arrow. Trivial means also in $W$, cofibrant means that the initial map is a cofibration, and fibrant means that the terminal map is a fibration. Combinatorial means locally presentable with both weak factorization systems generated by small sets; locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$ by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. For every combinatorial model category $\mathcal M$ there exist a small ordinary category $D$, a small set $S$ of arrows in $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$, and a Quillen equivalence
$$L:L_S\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R.$$
Here $\mathsf{sSet}$ consists of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with Kan fibrations (right lifting against all horn inclusions), weak homotopy equivalences, and monomorphisms as cofibrations. The projective model structure on $\mathsf U(D)$ has objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. A simplicial model category is enriched, tensored and cotensored in simplicial sets, with the induced map of mapping spaces for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either input arrow is trivial. The left Bousfield localization $L_S\mathsf U(D)$ has the same cofibrations; its weak equivalences $f$ are precisely the maps for which $\operatorname{Map}^{h}(f,Z)$ is an equivalence of spaces for every projectively fibrant $S$-local $Z$. Here $S$-local means $\operatorname{Map}^{h}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{h}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$, and $\operatorname{Map}^{h}$ is computed by cofibrant replacement of the source and fibrant replacement of the target in the projective model structure. The localized model structure is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial. Left proper means that pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. The adjunction $L\dashv R$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations on the left, and for every cofibrant $A$ in its source and fibrant $Y$ in $\mathcal M$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. All sets and presentability conditions are relative to the smaller fixed universe.

proof.text: Unpack the displayed model-category conventions: the two weak factorization systems, retract and two-out-of-three axioms, functorial factorizations, and the definitions of trivial, cofibrant, fibrant, combinatorial, locally presentable, and Quillen adjunction are exactly the definitions stated in the item. The simplicial-set convention is the cited simplicial-set definition.

Dugger’s Proposition 3.3 supplies a small ordinary category $D$ and a homotopically surjective Quillen adjunction $L_0:\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R_0$; by the defining clause, every fibrant $X$ and cofibrant replacement of $R_0X$ give a weak-equivalence composite to $X$.

The projective simplicial-presheaf model-structure theorem gives the objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations on $\mathsf U(D)$ and supplies completeness, cocompleteness, combinatoriality, simplicial enrichment, and left properness, together with the stated mapping-space axiom.

source.place: Example A.3.2.18 and Remark A.3.2.17 (printed p. 863); Proposition A.2.8.2 and Remarks A.2.8.4-A.2.8.5 (pp. 830-832); Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5 (pp. 870-871). Left properness follows by the objectwise cofibration and pushout descriptions. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Apply the homotopically surjective localization criterion to $L_0:\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R_0$. Its source is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial by Step 3, its target is combinatorial by hypothesis, and its counit hypothesis is exactly Step 2. It gives a small set $S$ of arrows and a Quillen equivalence $L:L_S\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R$ with these same adjoint functors.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 and proof of Theorem 1.1, printed pp. 181-182.

proof.text: To apply the localization-properties theorem, replace the small set $S$ by a small set $T$ of cofibrations as follows. For each $s:A\to B$ take a cofibrant replacement $q_A:QA\to A$ and factor $sq_A$ as a cofibration $i_s:QA\to B_s$ followed by a trivial fibration $p_s:B_s\to B$. Since $QA$ is cofibrant and $i_s$ is a cofibration, $B_s$ is cofibrant as well. The commutative square $(q_A,p_s):i_s\to s$ has weak-equivalence vertical arrows. The cited simplicial-model localization comparison identifies derived mapping spaces naturally with mapping spaces in the infinity localization; there these vertical arrows are equivalences, and precomposition therefore gives equivalences on mapping spaces into every $Z$. Thus the induced square of derived mapping spaces has equivalence vertical arrows. Hence $Z$ is $S$-local exactly when it is $T$-local for $T=\{i_s:s\in S\}$. Both endpoints of every member of $T$ are cofibrant, so for fibrant $Z$ their ordinary enriched mapping sets already compute the derived ones, by the same comparison. Apply the cited localization-existence theorem to $\mathcal M=\mathsf U(D)$ and this $T$; Step 3 supplies all three structural hypotheses. It constructs a left proper, combinatorial, simplicial model structure with unchanged cofibrations and weak equivalences detected by the original projectively fibrant $S$-local objects. This is the model structure $L_S\mathsf U(D)$ of Step 4: both have those same cofibrations and weak equivalences by the definition of localization, and fibrations are determined by the right lifting property against trivial cofibrations. Here originally fibrant means projectively fibrant; locality is an additional condition.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 (printed pp. 908-910), restricted to a small set of cofibrations between cofibrant objects; its proof constructs functorial local fibrant replacement. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: The left adjoint in Step 4 preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations because that adjunction is Quillen; its Quillen-equivalence property is precisely the displayed weak-equivalence test for a cofibrant $A$ and fibrant $Y$. The mapping-space axiom in Step 3 reads $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ for $i:A\to B$ and $p:X\to Y$; Step 5 supplies the same simplicial structure and the axiom for the localized cofibrations and fibrations. Its definition of locality and its computation of $\operatorname{Map}^{h}$ use replacements in the original projective structure, exactly as required in the item. These are expansions of the cited results and definitions, completing every clause.

split_report.summary: Six steps follow Dugger Propositions 3.3 and 3.2, using two new strict intermediate statements. Existing projective-model and Bousfield-localization nodes supply the structural inputs. Step 5 checks cofibrant endpoints of the replacement relations and uses the existing simplicial-model nerve comparison to identify the local-object classes. All citation quotations are current. The item statement retains its previously repaired universe and simplicial-set convention wording, without changing its mathematical assertion.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: the small simplicial-presheaf presentation used to supply the combinatorial model-category input before the coherent mapping-complex adjunction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q13-d51f2a7ef (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes (lem-coef-dugger-homotopically-surjective-map and lem-coef-dugger-localization-criterion) and the full statements of every cited node: simplicial-presheaf-projective-model, simplicial-bousfield-model-structure, simplicial-model-nerve-localization, kan-quillen-right-proper, complete-algebroid and the simplicial-set definition. Dugger, HTT and HA are not in literature/ and network access is blocked here, so I checked the statements against my knowledge of Dugger 2001 rather than the PDF: Thm 1.1, Def 3.1, Props 3.2 and 3.3, with UC carrying the projective structure. The item matches Thm 1.1 with no hypothesis added to the target, and the Quillen pair runs from L_S U(D) to M. Step 2 takes exactly Prop 3.3's conclusion. Step 3 gets the left proper, combinatorial, simplicial projective structure from the existing node. Step 4's hypotheses are each met: the source by Step 3, the target by hypothesis, the counit condition word for word by Step 2. Step 5 replaces each arrow s by a cofibration between cofibrant objects; the nerve node's comparison makes S-local and T-local agree, and since a model structure is fixed by its cofibrations and weak equivalences, the Bousfield node's structure is the L_S U(D) of Step 4. Steps 1 and 6 are genuinely elementary. Both new statements are true (the criterion also checks out at the infinity-category level through accessible reflective localization) and strictly smaller than the item. They state only, are self-contained, have single TeX escapes and correct provenance and blueprint fields, and record logged leanfinder, loogle and grep searches with no Mathlib match. Searching the DAG and the blueprint for Dugger, homotopically surjective and Bousfield found no duplicates; the second reading had already dropped the two earlier duplicate children. There is no cycle, the route stays inside sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, no tool_uses are needed, and no SGA source is cited. Small cases checked: sSet with D a point, the terminal category with D empty, empty or identity S, the arrow from the empty set to a point, the identity adjunction, a non-simplicial target such as Ch(Z), and the horn ranges. No fixes were made. The remaining caveat is the unarchived sources, already covered by the report's WANTED lines.
